_comment: NOT A SHIPPING CATALOG. This is the red-proof for R-96t and R-96v in scripts/check-forbidden.sh: one violation of each kind the pair can name, in the shape of a String Catalog, so that a gate run watches both checks fail as well as pass. A lint whose failure nobody has ever seen is a lint nobody has evidence for. Nothing loads this file at runtime and no bundle carries it; the keys use real deck names on purpose, because the fold's scope is read from NudgeVoice.swift and a fixture with invented deck names would be skipped rather than rejected. Do not fix these lines.

nudge.attention.waiting.comment: VIOLATION (R-96t): a second-person possessive outside the deck matrix, so the fold is proved to reach nudge.attention.* as well.

nudge.neutral.accusation.panel.body.comment: VIOLATION (R-96t): the person as grammatical subject, with the typographic apostrophe the catalog really ships, so the check is proved to normalise it.

nudge.neutral.accusation.panel.title.comment: VIOLATION (R-96v): an accusation wearing a question mark.

nudge.neutral.query.panel.title.comment: VIOLATION (R-96v): a question that does not ask.
